jobs.title: Maintenance Technician - Boise, ID
jobs.description_text: Role Overview As a Maintenance Technician, you ensure the community remains safe, functional, and well‑maintained by diagnosing and repairing a wide range of building and apartment systems. You provide timely, high‑quality service to residents, support preventative maintenance programs, and help preserve the property’s physical assets through consistent care and attention. Diagnose, repair, and resolve maintenance issues involving electrical, plumbing, HVAC systems, appliances, flooring, stairs, railings, and other building components. Schedule and perform preventative maintenance on HVAC units, equipment, and building systems to improve performance and reduce downtime. Maintain appropriate inventory of supplies and spare parts to ensure timely completion of work orders. Respond to on ‑ call rotations and emergency maintenance situations, assisting with both resident and property needs. Provide friendly, professional service when interacting with residents and team members. Document completed work and report recurring issues or safety concerns to your supervisor. Qualifications EPA certification required (Type I, II, or Universal). 1–3+ years of experience in maintenance, facilities

jobs.description_text: About The Role Autonomous driving software today improves mostly by hand: engineers collect data, train models, and tune modules. This role explores a different approach, in which AI agents take part in that work. Agents propose changes to policy code, data, training recipes, or model code. They then evaluate the results, diagnose failures, and turn verified fixes into reusable skills and data for the next round. With DiDi Voyager's real-world driving data and large-scale evaluation infrastructure, the goal is a loop that produces improvements that generalize across scenarios, pass safety gates, and reach the vehicle. The role combines machine learning, agentic systems, and autonomous driving, and will help shape both the onboard architecture and how driving software is developed. Agents get permissioned access to the driving stack, data, training infrastructure, and evaluation environments, along with automatic scenario setup and pass/fail checks, so they can run experiments without a person in every step. Develop recursive self-improvement (RSI) loops. These include failure mining, candidate generation, evolutionary search, and targeted data generation aimed at the policy's current weaknesses. jobs.description_text: OVERVIEW We are seeking a highly motivated WMS Business Systems Analyst to support the implementation, optimization, and ongoing administration of Manhattan Active Warehouse Management (WM). This role serves as a key liaison between warehouse operations, business stakeholders, Technology, and vendor partners. The ideal candidate combines strong business process knowledge with technical aptitude and hands-on experience configuring and supporting warehouse management systems. The role will be responsible for translating operational requirements into system capabilities, documenting business processes, developing functional specifications, supporting testing activities, and managing configuration changes within the Warehouse Management System (WMS). Following implementation, this individual will have ownership of the platform's configuration management lifecycle, including configuration design, deployment management, testing coordination, release preparedness, and production promotion activities. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys operating at the intersection of business process design, system configuration, solution delivery, and continuous improvement. RESPONSIBILITIES Business Process Analysis & Requirements Management Partner with warehouse operations, inventory management, transportation, customer service, and supply chain stakeholders to understand business needs.
